text:
Leah (CS): Quick pulse on NimbusPay after week 3 of onboarding. Traffic steady ~11.8k req/day. Observed: p50 ~170ms, p95 ~820ms, sporadic errors on >900-token outputs. Cost per long response sliding up; customer called latency a risk for renewals. Thinking proactive optimization before renewal.

Sam (CS Manager): Agree we should be proactive. Put together a low-risk experiment plan we can present in the renewal packet.

Devon (SE): TL;DR plan request: which levers and how invasive. Can we try routing + caching first before quantizing?

Mira (Applied ML): Proposed sequence: 1) deploy output-length based routing to route predicted long outputs to redwood-compact-6b; 2) enable prefix (KV) caching for common templates; 3) run a conservative int8 profile on the current model in parallel (offline) and only enable if canary looks clean. Routing + caching alone should hit ~18-25% GPU-time reduction on long-form flows.

Ivy (SRE): what about tail latency regressions on cache misses? need a fallback path and an automated rollback if errors or quality regress.

Leah (CS): customer comms: i'll draft a note that we may serve some long outputs from a compact model during the trial window and explain why + how to flag UX issues. want to avoid surprises.

Mira (Applied ML): Eval plan: 150 targeted prompts focusing on long-doc generation, table serialization, and instruction-following edge cases. Metrics: embedding cosine >=0.915 vs oracle + automated precision checks for extracted entities. Tolerance: <=2% increase in hallucination flags, <=1% uplift in structured-output failures.

Devon (SE): I'll own the routing feature flag + rollout. Suggest canary_fraction: 0.10 for 72 hours to get enough samples on long outputs. Quality gate: embedding_cosine_min 0.915, max_hallucination_pct_increase 2.0.

Sam (CS Manager): Can we make the canary selective: only route requests predicted >700 tokens AND from non-critical endpoints? keeps risk lower.

Devon (SE): Yes. We'll target /chat/long-doc and /reports/generate paths. Predictive model uses fast token-count estimator.

Ivy (SRE): scheduling: recommend off-peak deploy window tonight 0200-0400 UTC. Also add alerting on error-rate >5% or p95 increase >25% compared to baseline.

Mira (Applied ML): Timeline estimate: routing + caching config + regression harness automation: ~2 dev-days (shared). Int8 offline profiling & validation: ~1 dev-day. If canary passes, enabling int8 on dedicated pool is another ~0.5 day ops work.

Devon (SE): rollout YAML snippet (feature-flag driven):

```yaml
route: /chat/long-doc
predictive_threshold: 700
fallback_model: redwood-compact-6b
canary:
  fraction: 0.10
  duration_hours: 72
quality_gate:
  embedding_cosine_min: 0.915
  max_hallucination_increase_pct: 2.0
alerts:
  - on: error_rate
    threshold_pct: 5
  - on: p95_latency
    threshold_increase_pct: 25
```

Sam (CS Manager): Nice. For the renewal story, we should aim to show projected cost delta (conservative) of 20-30% and an operational risk plan (canary + rollback + customer opt-out).

Leah (CS): Action items: 1) Mira produce eval set + run baseline (24h) 2) Devon implement flag + deploy canary (tonight) 3) Ivy add alerts + monitor dashboards 4) Leah send customer pre-notice and gather permission for trial on non-critical endpoints.

deploy-bot: Created ticket CS-4892: "NimbusPay cost-smoothing probe: routing + caching canary" -> https://redwood.internal/tickets/CS-4892 :white_check_mark:

Ivy (SRE): I'll add a datadog dashboard and an automated smoke test hitting sample prompts every 10m during canary.

Mira (Applied ML): Will share eval results and a short README for the regression checks when done. If compact fallback shows any structured-output drop, we'll hold off quantization.

Devon (SE): Once we have canary numbers, we'll decide whether to advance int8 plan. If routing + caching alone hits target, present that first to renewals.

Leah (CS): Thanks team. I'll circulate the customer note draft and a one-pager for renewals with the conservative cost-savings estimate. Catch up after the 72h canary. :thumbsup:
